{{nihongo|'''Ohari Shrine'''|尾針神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Bizen Province]].

=== Enshrined deities ===
; Principal deity
* '''{{ill|Amenohoakari|fr|Ame-no-hoakari|it|Amenohoakari|ja|天火明命|ko|아메노호아카리|mni|ꯑꯃꯦꯅꯣꯍꯣꯑꯀꯔꯤ|simple|Ame-no-hoakari|zh|天火明命|qid=Q10940411}}''' - ancestral deity of the {{ill|Owari clan|Q11465311|qid=Q11465311}}

; Associated deity
* {{ill|Ōgetsuhime|es|Ōgetsuhime|ja|オオゲツヒメ|zh|大宜都比賣|qid=Q3261482|lt=Ogetsuhime-no-Mikoto}}

Regarding the deity, ''{{ill|Kibi Onko Hiroku|ja|吉備温故秘録|qid=Q11412654}}'' also presents theories identifying it as Otsunane-no-Mikoto or {{ill|Yamato Takeru|Q461258|qid=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto}}<ref name="神々"/>.

=== History ===
The shrine stands on a hill to the east-west side of central Okayama. Behind the shrine buildings remains a group of giant rocks regarded as a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=iwasaka}}, and {{ill|Haji pottery|Q5639938|qid=Q5639938}} and {{ill|Sue pottery|Q7634351|qid=Q7634351}} have been excavated from the eastern slope<ref name="神々"/>, indicating long-term habitation.

Its founding is unknown, but the area was formerly called "Ifuku-go, Mino District, {{ill|Kingdom of Kibi|de|Provinz Kibi|ff|Kibi Province|fr|Province de Kibi|it|Kibi (provincia)|ja|吉備国|ko|기비국|nl|Kibi (provincie)|pt|Província de Kibi|simple|Kibi Province|zh|吉備國|zh_min_nan|Kibi-kok|qid=Q1155128}}," and is said to have been the settlement of the Ifukube no Muraji (a branch of the {{ill|Owari clan|Q11465311|qid=Q11465311|lt=Owari no Muraji}}). The shrine is said to have begun by enshrining their ancestral deity, Ame-no-Hoakari-no-Mikoto<ref>[http://www.okayama-jinjacho.or.jp/cgi-bin/jsearch.cgi?mode=detail&jcode=01091 Ohari Shrine] (Okayama Prefectural Association of Shinto Shrines).</ref>. Nearby stands another shikinaisha connected to the Owari clan, {{ill|Ojiharina Mawakahime Shrine|ja|尾治針名真若比咩神社|qid=Q17228003}}, suggesting a relationship with that clan. There are theories that the Ifukube migrated west from Owari<ref>Recorded in the Meiji-era ''Engishiki Naijinsha / Kokushi Genzai no Jinja'' ("Ohari Shrine" section in ''Nihon no Kamigami'').</ref>, and conversely theories that the Owari clan migrated east from Kibi to Owari<ref>Hiroaki Shimoyama, "Did the ancient Owari clan migrate east from Kibi?" (''Okayama Prefecture Mystery Walk'', Shinjinbutsu Bunko).</ref>.

In the mid-{{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}, the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}'' lists "Ohari Shrine, Mino District, {{ill|Bizen Province|bn|বাইজেন প্রদেশ|cs|Provincie Bizen|de|Provinz Bizen|es|Provincia de Bizen|fa|ولایت بیزن|fr|Province de Bizen|gl|Provincia de Bizen|id|Provinsi Bizen|it|Bizen (provincia)|ja|備前国|ko|비젠국|lt|Bidzeno žemė|nl|Bizen (provincie)|pt|Província de Bizen|ru|Бидзэн (провинция)|simple|Bizen Province|sk|Bizen (provincia)|sr|Провинција Бизен|tr|Bizen (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Бідзен|zh|備前國|zh_min_nan|Bizen-kok|qid=Q1053688}}" as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and this shrine is considered one of its {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|Q135022904|qid=Q135022904}}. In the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, the exact location of that shikinaisha was said to be unknown<ref name="神々"/>, and some documents of that era state that the shrine land of Sakaori-no-miya (now {{ill|Okayama Shrine|ja|岡山神社|zh|岡山神社|qid=Q11048799}}) was the original precinct<ref name="神々"/>. Even now, Ohari Shrine is enshrined among the subordinate shrines of Okayama Shrine, and is regarded as another disputed identification.

Until the early Meiji period it was called "Kurioka-no-miya"<ref name="神々">''Nihon no Kamigami'', section on Ohari Shrine.</ref>. In Meiji it was renamed "Ohari Shrine." Under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=modern shrine ranking system}}, it was ranked a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}.
